The interpreted maṣdar (أن يذّكّر) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to what the interpreted maṣdar (لينذروا) is attached to, because it is conjoined to it.

safi-cedvel:31-31.t:
* I'rab:
(قل) like the preceding «1» , (لعبادي) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (قل) , and the sign of the genitive is the kasra implied on the letter before the yāʾ.. and (الياء) is muḍāf ilayhi (الذين) a relative in the position of a genitive, naʿt of عباد (آمنوا) like بدّلوا «2» .. and the object of قلّ is omitted, implied "establish the prayer" (يقيموا) an imperfect verb, jussive as the answer to the request of the implied verb أقيموا, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and (الواو) is the agent (الصلاة) direct object, accusative (الواو) a conjunction (ينفقوا) like يقيموا and conjoined to it (من) a preposition (ما) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of a genitive, attached to (ينفقوا) , and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "that We have provided them with" (رزقناهم) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (نا) is the agent, and (هم) the direct object (سرّا) a verbal noun in the place of a ḥāl, accusative [Note: or a mafʿūl muṭlaq standing in for the verbal noun because it is its kind, i.e. "spending in secret".] , (علانية) conjoined to (سرّا) with the wāw, accusative (من قبل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يقيموا) or (ينفقوا) , (أن) a maṣdar particle (يأتي) an imperfect verb, accusative (يوم) agent, nominative (لا) negative (بيع) mubtadaʾ, nominative [Note: or the noun of (لا) operating like ليس, and the khabar of لا is the preposition and its genitive noun "فيه".] , (في) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to the khabar (الواو) a conjunction (لا) redundant, to reinforce the negation (خلال) conjoined to بيع, nominative like it.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن يأتي ... ) is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
Clause: «قل ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «آمنوا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين) .
And the clause: «يقيموا ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of an implied condition, not accompanied by the fāʾ, i.e. "if they are commanded to establish the prayer, they will establish it".
And the clause: «ينفقوا ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause يقيموا.
And the clause: «رزقناهم ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (ما) .
And the clause: «يأتي يوم ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-like (أن) .
And the clause: «لا بيع فيه ... » is in the position of a nominative, naʿt of يوم.

* Morphology:
(خلال) , a samāʿī (heard-from-the-Arabs) verbal noun of the quadriliteral خالّه, i.e. "he befriended him"; its pattern is فعال with kasra on the fāʾ, and it is singular.. or it is the plural of خلة with kasra on the khāʾ, meaning befriending and brotherhood.

* Rhetoric:
- Omission of the content of the saying:
Regarding the saying of the Exalted قُلْ لِعِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا.. etc., most of the parsers agreed that the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) is omitted, indicated by its answer, i.e. "Say to them: Establish the prayer and spend". The skilled rejected this parsing, saying: "There is something to consider in this parsing, because the answer would then be a report; for if he said this saying to them, they would comply with its requirement and establish the prayer and spend; yet they were told, and many of them did not comply, and the report of Allah is too exalted for contradiction. This subtlety is what led many of the parsers to turn away from this parsing, despite its leaping to mind at first glance. Its correctness is possible by taking the general as the majority rather than as all-inclusive. It is strengthened by two fine points: one is that this construction occurs only for one described with true faith, whose faith is lauded at the time of the command, like this verse and others, such as the saying of the Exalted قُلْ لِعِبادِي يَقُولُوا الَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ and وقُلْ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَغُضُّوا مِنْ أَبْصارِهِمْ وَيَحْفَظُوا فُرُوجَهُمْ. The second is its repeated occurrence for those described as servants of Allah, honoured by their being annexed to the name of Allah the Exalted. They have said that the word العباد occurs in the Mighty Book only as praise of the believers, especially when the Exalted is annexed to it with the annexation of honour. The sum is that the one commanded in this verse is one who is on the point of compliance and in the sphere of hastening to obedience, so the report of their compliance is true and sound, either in general if that is intended, or for the majority."

The attribution of misguiding to them is figurative because they are inanimate and nothing of that is conceivable from them; the one who misguides in reality is Allah the Exalted. It may also be a free metonymy (majāz mursal) whose relation is causation, because they are a cause of misguidance.
2- Antithesis (ṭibāq): in several forms, such as the saying of the Exalted رَبَّنا إِنَّكَ تَعْلَمُ ما نُخْفِي وَما نُعْلِنُ وما يَخْفى عَلَى اللَّهِ مِنْ شَيْءٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلا فِي السَّماءِ.

1- «ربّ» is a vocative annexed to the yāʾ of the first person.
The vocative, by i'rab, is of two kinds:
1- Indeclinable on the ḍamma in the position of an accusative. This is the singular proper name and the specific indefinite noun.
2- Declinable, accusative. This is the non-specific indefinite noun, the annexed noun, and the noun resembling the annexed. Thus the kinds of vocative are five: singular proper name, specific indefinite, non-specific indefinite, annexed, and resembling the annexed; and the muḍāf ilayhi, which is the yāʾ, has been omitted.
A parallel to it has already been treated, so return to it in its proper places.

* Rhetoric:

The use of "standing" in what is mentioned is either a free metonymy (majāz mursal) or a metaphor, and among that is "the war stood". It is also allowed that the reckoning be likened to a standing man by implicit metaphor (istiʿāra makniyya), with standing affirmed for it by imaginative attribution (takhyīl), or that what is meant is "the people of the reckoning stand", the muḍāf being omitted, or what belongs to its people is attributed to the reckoning figuratively.

* Benefits:
The building of the Kaʿba: Ibrāhīm confided to his son Ismāʿīl an awesome secret and a wondrous command; he said to him: "O my son, Allah has commanded me to build a house here.."

Ismāʿīl was preparing the tools and bringing the stones while Ibrāhīm raised the building. Then Ibrāhīm said: "O my son, find me a stone to place under my feet, that I may be able to complete what I began and oversee what I have built." Ismāʿīl came upon the Black Stone and presented it to his father, who stood on it building, while Ismāʿīl handed him the stones and moved around the structure until the building of the House was completed, which became a resort for the people. [Translator's note: the source prints «حيث أقام عليه بيني» ("where he stood on it, building me"), which seems to be a slip for «يبني».] And Allah answered Ibrāhīm's prayer: فَاجْعَلْ أَفْئِدَةً مِنَ النَّاسِ تَهْوِي إِلَيْهِمْ وَارْزُقْهُمْ مِنَ الثَّمَراتِ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَشْكُرُونَ, Sūrat Ibrāhīm, verse 38.

safi-cedvel:42-43.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (لا) prohibitive, jussive-governing (تحسبنّ) an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa, in the position of a jussive, and the agent is "you", and (النون) is for emphasis (الله) the divine name, first direct object, accusative (غافلا) second direct object, accusative (عن) a preposition (ما) a maṣdar particle [Note: or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, the clause after it being the ṣila, and the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "the wrongdoers do".] (يعمل) an imperfect verb, nominative (الظالمون) agent, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw (إنّما) a restrictive particle (kāffa) and the restricted (يؤخّرهم) like يعمل ... and (هم) a pronoun, direct object, and the agent is "he" (ليوم) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (يؤخّر) , (تشخص..
الأبصار) like يعمل الظالمون (في) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (تشخص) .
Clause: «لا تحسبنّ ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «يعمل الظّالمون ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the particle-like (ما) and the interpreted maṣdar (ما يعمل ... ) is in the position of a genitive by the preposition, attached to (غافلا) and the clause: «يؤخّرهم ... » has no grammatical position, a clarifying resumption.
And the clause: «تشخص فيه الأبصار ... » is in the position of a genitive, naʿt of يوم.
(مهطعين) a ḥāl, accusative, from الأبصار because it indicates their owners, and the sign of the accusative is the yāʾ [Note: or a direct object of an omitted verb, implied "you see them", the seeing then being of the heart; or a ḥāl from the pronoun in (تراهم) , the seeing then being visual.] , (مقنعي) a second ḥāl, accusative, like معطهين [Translator's note: the source prints «معطهين» for مهطعين.] (رؤوسهم) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive, and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi (لا) a particle of negation (يرتدّ) like يعمل (إلى) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached - (يرتدّ) , [Translator's note: the source breaks off at «متعلق-» before «(يرتدّ)».] (طرفهم) agent, nominative, and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction (أفئده) mubtadaʾ, nominative and (هم) like the last (هواء) khabar, nominative.
And the clause: «لا يرتدّ إليهم طرفهم ... » is in the position of an accusative, ḥāl from the pronoun in مقنعي [Note: or it is a badal of مقنعي.] .
And the clause: «أفئدتهم هواء ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause لا يرتدّ ... [Note: or it is a ḥāl without conjunction, its operator being what operates in the preceding ḥāl, or it is resumptive with no position.] .

* Morphology:
(مهطعين) , plural of مهطع, an active participle from أهطع in the sense of "hurried". Its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.
(مقنعي) , plural of مقنع, its nūn dropped because of annexation, an active participle like مهطع, its pattern is مفعل.
(طرف) , originally a verbal noun, then applied to the faculty of sight; its pattern is فعل with fatḥa then sukūn.
(هواء) , originally a rigid noun, used here as an adjective meaning empty or void; for this reason the sense of the tāʾ that indicates plurality is implied in it and it remained singular; its pattern is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ.. The final hamza is changed from yāʾ because it is pluralised as أهوية; when the yāʾ came final after a quiescent alif it was turned into hamza.

* Benefits:
1- عَمَّا يَعْمَلُ الظَّالِمُونَ: When the preposition «عن» enters the relative «ما», it is written with the alif, as in this verse. When it enters an interrogative noun, the alif is dropped and it is written with the mīm only, as in the saying of the Exalted: عَمَّ يَتَساءَلُونَ؟ ..
2- (مهطعين) : a ḥāl, and the ḥāl is an indefinite accusative noun that explains the state of the agent or the direct object, or both together at the occurrence of the action.
An example of a ḥāl explaining the state of the agent is: (سأزحف ثائرا متمردا) ("I shall advance, rebelling, defiant"), and of the object: (ركب عليّ السيارة مسرعة) ("ʿAlī rode the car, speeding").
Kinds of ḥāl: a- The singular ḥāl: that which is neither a clause nor a quasi-clause, and agrees with its ṣāḥib in gender (masculine and feminine) and in number (singular, dual and plural), such as: (واجه الصّعاب قويا) ("he faced the difficulties, strong"), (واجها الصّعاب قويين) ("the two faced the difficulties, strong"), (واجهوا الصّعاب أقوياء) ("they faced the difficulties, strong").
b- The quasi-clause ḥāl, which comes as an attached element (adverb or preposition and its genitive noun), such as: (الصيف على الجبال أجمل منه على الشاطئ) ("Summer on the mountains is more beautiful than on the shore").
c- The ḥāl as a clause (nominal or verbal), such as: رأيت زيدا وهو خارج ("I saw Zayd while he was going out"), and رأيت زيدا يخرج ("I saw Zayd going out").
It is required of a clause occurring as a ḥāl that it contain a link tying it to the ṣāḥib al-ḥāl, and this link may be:
(1) the wāw alone, such as: (لن نفعل والعدوّ متربص) ("We shall not do it while the enemy lies in wait").
(2) or the pronoun alone, such as: (جئت وقد هبط الظلام) ("I came when darkness had fallen").
(3) or the pronoun and the wāw together, such as: لا تَقْرَبُوا الصَّلاةَ وَأَنْتُمْ سُكارى.

safi-cedvel:44-45.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (أنذر) an imperative verb, and the agent is "you" (الناس) direct object, accusative (يوم) second direct object, accusative, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "warn them of its terrors" (يأتيهم) an imperfect verb, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the ḍamma implied on the yāʾ, and (هم) a pronoun, direct object, (العذاب) agent, nominative (الفاء) a conjunction (يقول) like يأتي (الذين) a relative noun, indeclinable in the position of a nominative, agent (ظلموا) a past verb and its agent (ربّنا) its i'rab has been given earlier [Note: In verse (37) of this sūra.] , (أخّرنا) , like انذر.. and (نا) a pronoun, direct object (إلى أجل) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (أخّرنا) , (قريب) naʿt of أجل, genitive (نجب) an imperfect verb, jussive, the answer to the request, and the agent is "we" (دعوتك) direct object, accusative.. and (الكاف) muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction (نتّبع الرسل) like نجب دعوتك, and the end of the verb was given a kasra because of the meeting of two quiescents (الهمزة) for interrogation (الواو) a conjunction (لم) a particle of negation and jussive (تكونوا) a defective imperfect verb, jussive, the sign of the jussive being the dropping of the nūn ... and (الواو) is the noun of تكون (أقسمتم) a past verb, indeclinable on the sukūn.. and (تم) is a pronoun, agent (ما) negative (اللام) a preposition and (كم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to a preposed khabar (من) a redundant preposition (زوال) genitive in form, nominative in position, a postposed mubtadaʾ.
Clause: «أنذر الناس ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «يأتيهم العذاب ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «يقول الذين ... » is in the position of a genitive, conjoined to the clause يأتيهم العذاب.
And the clause: «ظلموا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين) .
And the clause: «النّداء وجوابها ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).
And the clause: «أخّرنا ... » has no grammatical position, the answer to the vocative.
And the clause: «نجب ... » has no grammatical position, the apodosis of an implied condition, not accompanied by the fāʾ.
And the clause: «نتّبع ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the clause نجب..
And the clause: «لم تكونوا ... » is in the position of an accusative, the content of an implied saying..
And the clause: «القول المقدّرة معطوفة على جملة يقول الذين ظلموا. [Translator's note: the source text of this clause is incomplete as printed, lacking the closing guillemet and the opening «وجملة» of the implied clause; it reads "the implied saying clause is conjoined to the clause يقول الذين ظلموا".]
And the clause: «أقسمتم ... » is in the position of an accusative, khabar of تكونوا.
And the clause: «ما لكم من زوال ... » has no grammatical position, the answer to the oath.
(الواو) a conjunction (سكنتم) like أقسمتم (في مساكن) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (سكنتم) , (الّذين) a relative, muḍāf ilayhi (ظلموا) like the first (أنفسهم) direct object, accusative.. and (هم) muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) resumptive (تبيّن) a past verb and the agent is omitted, understood from the context of the speech, i.e. "their state became clear" (كيف) an interrogative noun, indeclinable in the position of an accusative, ḥāl, its operator being (فعلنا) which is a verb and agent (الباء) a preposition and (هم) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (فعلنا) , (الواو) resumptive (ضربنا) like فعلنا (لكم) like the first, attached to (ضربنا) , (الأمثال) direct object, accusative.
And the clause: «سكنتم ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause أقسمتم [Note: it may be a ḥāl with an implied قد.] .
And the clause: «ظلموا ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the relative noun (الّذين) .
And the clause: «تبيّن لكم (الحال) ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «فعلنا ... » has no grammatical position, a clarifying resumption.
And the clause: «ضربنا ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.

* Morphology:
(زوال) a verbal noun of the triliteral زال, its pattern is فعال with fatḥa on the fāʾ; there are other verbal nouns, among them زول with fatḥa and sukūn, and زوالان on the pattern فعلان with two fatḥas.

safi-cedvel:46-48.t:
* I'rab:
(الواو) resumptive (قد) a particle of certainty (مكروا) a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma ... and (الواو) is the agent (مكرهم) mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), accusative [Note: Abū Ḥayyān said: "What is preserved is that مكر is not made transitive to a direct object by itself; the Exalted said: وإذ يمكر بك الذين كفروا, and 'Zayd is مكور' is not preserved; rather one says 'ممكور به'." End.] . (هم) muḍāf ilayhi (الواو) a conjunction (عند) an adverb, accusative, attached to an omitted preposed khabar (الله) the divine name, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (مكرهم) a postposed mubtadaʾ, nominative, with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "the recompense for their plotting" or "the knowledge of their plotting".. and (هم) like the first (الواو) resumptive (إن) negative [Note: or lightened from (إنّ) , i.e. "they plotted to remove what is equal to the mountains in firmness, but they were unable to do so". It is conditional in the opinion of Ibn Hishām.] , (كان) a defective past verb - an abrogator [Note: or it is complete, i.e. "their plot did not exist so that the laws and prophethoods, which are like the mountains in their firmness, would pass away by it."] - (مكرهم) the noun of kāna, nominative, and (هم) like the first (اللام) the lām of cause [Note: Ibn Hishām rejected that the lām be the lām of denial (juḥūd), and said in brief: "There is something to consider in this statement, because the particle of negation is other than (ما) or (لم), and the agents of (كان) and (تزول) differ.. The apparent is that it is the lām of purpose (lām kay) and (إن) is conditional, i.e.: with Allah is the recompense of their plotting, and it is a greater plot than theirs, even if their plot, by its intensity, was prepared for the removal of great matters likened in their greatness to mountains." End; the apodosis of the condition is omitted, indicated by what precedes, i.e. "so with Allah is the recompense of their plotting".] , (تزول) an imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām (من) a preposition and (الهاء) a pronoun in the position of a genitive, attached to (تزول) and من is causal (الجبال) agent, nominative.
And the interpreted maṣdar (أن تزول) is in the position of a genitive, attached to an omitted khabar of كان [Note: or attached to the complete (كان) .] .
Clause: «قد مكروا ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive.
And the clause: «عند الله مكرهم ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to the resumptive clause.
And the clause: «كان مكرهم..» has no grammatical position, resumptive. [Note: The meaning stated: their plot was not prepared to remove mountains; and it is an illustration of the affair of the Messenger ﷺ.]
And the clause: «تزول منه الجبال ... » has no grammatical position, the ṣila of the implied particle-like (أن) .
(الفاء) a conjunction linking the effect to the cause [Note: or a connecting particle for an implied conditional apodosis.] , (لا تحسبنّ الله مخلف) like ولا تحسبنّ الله غافلا [Note: In verse (42) of this sūra.] , (وعده) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.. and (الهاء) muḍāf ilayhi (رسله) first direct object of the active participle مخلف, which is annexed to its second object وعد [Note: If (مخلف) is made transitive to one, then (رسل) is the object of the verbal noun وعد.] and (الهاء) like the last (إنّ) a particle of emphasis and accusative (الله) the divine name, the noun of inna (عزيز) khabar of inna, nominative (ذو) a second khabar, nominative, the sign of the nominative being the wāw (انتقام) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive.
And the clause: «لا تحسبنّ ... » has no grammatical position, conjoined to an implied clause, i.e. "be alert, so do not think".. or conjoined to the preceding resumptive clause قد مكروا ... [Note: or it is the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e.: if the state of the wrongdoers is such in plotting, then do not think that Allah ...] .
And the clause: «إنّ الله عزيز ... » has no grammatical position, causal.
(يوم) an adverb of time, accusative, attached to انتقام [Note: or attached to مخلف وعده رسله.. and inna and what follows is parenthetical. Or it is a direct object of an omitted verb, implied "remember".] , (تبدّل) a passive imperfect verb, nominative (الأرض) deputy agent, nominative (غير) direct object, accusative [Note: and it is originally an adjective of an omitted noun, i.e. "an earth other than the earth".] , (الأرض) muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (الواو) a conjunction (السموات) conjoined to the deputy agent, nominative (الواو) resumptive (برزوا) like مكروا (لله) a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (برزوا) with an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "for the recompense of Allah" (الواحد) naʿt of the divine name, genitive (القهّار) a second naʿt, genitive.
And the clause: «تبدّل الأرض ... » is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
And the clause: «برزوا ... » has no grammatical position, resumptive [Note: al-Jamal allows it to be conjoined to the clause تبدّل, making the past in the sense of the imperfect, i.e. "and the Day they come forth to Allah ..."] , or a ḥāl with an implied قد.

* Morphology:
(مخلف) , an active participle of the quadriliteral أخلف, its pattern is مفعل with ḍamma on the mīm and kasra on the ʿayn.

* Rhetoric:
- Explicit metaphor (istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya): in the saying of the Exalted وَإِنْ كانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لِتَزُولَ مِنْهُ الْجِبالُ, where by His saying لتزول منه الجبال their plot is likened to mountains for its enormity and intensity, their absorption in it and their reaching the utmost of it; and His law, His signs and the lofty teachings and clear proofs He sent down upon His Prophet are likened to mountains in their firmness and their being established in the souls of the believers.

* Benefits:
1- مُخْلِفَ وَعْدِهِ:
مخلف is the second direct object of the verb «تحسبنّ» and it is annexed. Had it been read detached from annexation, with tanwīn, «مخلفا وعده», it would operate as an active participle, and وعده would become the direct object of the active participle. There is a continuation of this discussion, which we shall give its due later on.
(2) يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ الْأَرْضُ غَيْرَ الْأَرْضِ.
The commentators and thinkers took various positions on the substitution; the most important are two:
The first is that the substitution is from one state to another with the original remaining as it is.
The second is that the substitution is the removal of a thing and its replacement by another.
